topomer.note: 50 of 114 molecules can be cut at the framework

findings.text: 47 chemotype(s); the largest holds 19 of 114 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 5 heavy atoms, about 26% of a typical molecule, and 44% of the set can be cut at it
the 5 shared framework atoms sit 0.1 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (59 of 114 carry them)
the aligned model is -0.056 in q2 against counts (95% interval -0.179 to +0.052) -- the frame gains nothing over counts
the aligned model is -0.072 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.202 to +0.020) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is -0.042 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.286 to +0.162) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is -0.040 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval -0.170 to +0.065) -- descriptors alone do as well, so the geometry adds nothing on this set

why: descriptors alone match the 3D model, so a field model here is an expensive way to count atoms; use the fields only if the co-field is the purpose
